product_from_film: InsForge supplies backend services that a coding agent can operate through its CLI and skills to build an application.
explains_well: The example connects installation, an app request, a working screenshot interface and the resulting backend records.
unclear: The build itself is compressed between dense prompt/terminal views and the finished app; the viewer cannot easily separate setup, generation and deployment.
scenario: A presenter demonstrates connecting Claude Code to InsForge, requesting a screenshot service, using the app and inspecting its backend resources.
product_clear_basis: Install InsForge shows a CLI command and coding-agent options at 11–17s; the ASR opening explicitly identifies the backend role.

categories.finding: Platform overview → install → app prompt → signup/key → screenshot results → backend audit.
The dashboard opens immediately, making this a direct walkthrough; the visible opening lacks a concise benefit heading.
CLI, coding-agent options and the backend sidebar identify a developer audience. The draft clarifies the agent-operated backend role early.
Pointer movement, selected text, UI changes and zoomed screen crops guide the demonstration; exact zoom easing is unchecked.
The Example Walkthrough card clearly separates overview from the example. The later return to backend resources connects visible app behavior to its infrastructure.
Dark functional UI, purple app accents, monospaced terminal text and a consistent presenter inset dominate.
The enlarged terminal helps, but long prompts and small table labels still demand close reading. The inspected 43s full-resolution frame clarifies the app request.
A coherent ASR walkthrough supports the steps; garbled product names are resolved only from visible labels. Voice qualities are unassessed.

Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: The login, key creation and image results are understandable silently, but the distinction between backend product and generated Snap app needs labels.
Large pointer/crops help focus. Dense terminal content and the broad app frame compete with the small presenter inset.
Setup and terminal context occupy about half the film; the result sequence begins at 62s, followed by a long backend inventory.
The screenshot-service request pays off with two page images, then corresponding stored records and files.
The two results and backend inspection may create confidence through specificity; viewer trust is not measured.
Input, output and persistence are linked well. The actual generation interval and deployment steps are not fully shown.
The film shows two output images and backend resources. One-shot completeness, performance, deployment reliability and code quality were not independently tested.
The agent installation panel and backend-resource follow-through distinguish the example from a frontend-only demo.
Add clear stage labels and shorten static terminal/closing holds.
